caseStudies.title: Blomgram
caseStudies.summary: Blomgram is a global cross-border payment platform offering instant, affordable transfers and multi-currency financial tools for Africans worldwide.

sections.heading: The Problem
sections.body:
Cross-border money transfers can be stressful and difficult to navigate for Africans living, working, and doing business globally.

Business Problem

Blomgram needed to simplify and scale its cross-border payment experience while building trust and differentiating itself in a competitive fintech market.

User Problem

Users struggled with unclear fees, exchange rates, transaction status, and the complexity of sending and managing money across different currencies.

Existing Challenges

Existing cross-border payment experiences were often fragmented, complex, and lacked the transparency users needed to feel confident about their transactions.

cards.title: Amara Okafor
cards.body:
Product Manager

Age: 31

Location: London, UK

Goal: Send money home quickly and affordably while knowing exactly what the recipient will receive.
**Pain Points**
- Unclear transfer fees
- Confusing exchange rates
- Long or complicated transfer processes
- Limited visibility after sending money
**Needs**

Speed, transparency, affordability, and reliable transaction tracking.

cards.title: Daniel Mensah
cards.body:
Remote Software Consultant

Age: 31

Location: Accra, Ghana

Goal: Receive international payments and manage money across multiple currencies.
**Pain Points**
- Managing different currencies across multiple platforms
- Difficulty converting currencies efficiently
- Limited visibility into balances and transactions
**Needs**

A centralized multi-currency wallet, easy currency exchange, and clear financial insights.

cards.title: Chiamaka Eze
cards.body:
E-commerce Business Owner

Age: 31

Location:  Lagos, Nigeria

Goal: Receive and send international payments while keeping track of business transactions.
**Pain Points**
- High transaction costs
- Complicated international payment processes
- Difficulty tracking incoming and outgoing payments
- Lack of a unified financial platform
**Needs**

Affordable transfers, transparent costs, transaction history, and efficient payment management.

cards.title: 02 Build trust

cards.title: 03 Create a unified financial experience

sections.heading: Strict Modular Foundations
sections.body: Clean, utility-focused typographic scales, geometric color spaces, and composable UI blocks.

sections.heading: Signup and Sign in Experience
sections.body:
I designed Blomgram’s signup flow to make account creation simple, fast, and familiar. Users can sign up with Apple, Google, or their phone number, reducing the need for lengthy forms.

The goal was to minimize friction, build trust from the first interaction, and get users into the platform quickly while keeping the experience clean and intuitive.

sections.heading: User Onboarding & Verification
sections.body:
I structured the experience into clear, progressive steps—from country selection and email registration to OTP verification. The country selector was designed to scale as more markets are introduced, while reusable form components and consistent interaction patterns create a foundation for future onboarding requirements.

UX Focus
- Reduced cognitive load through a simple step-by-step flow.
- Clear hierarchy and familiar form interactions.
- Country selection designed for a growing international user base.
- OTP verification provides a focused, easy-to-complete authentication step.
- Clear feedback states distinguish between inactive and completed actions.
**Business Impact**

The design creates an onboarding foundation that can scale with geographic expansion and growing user base, while maintaining a consistent experience. The emphasis is on reducing onboarding friction, supporting user completion, and creating reusable patterns that make future product expansion more efficient.

sections.heading: DASHBOARD
sections.body:
**The Design Approach**

RESEARCH → DEFINE → DESIGN → TEST

I started with user research and competitor analysis to understand real user needs and pain points. Through interviews and usability insights, I identified the key goals: simple navigation, clear financial visibility, and trust in every transaction.

I then translated these insights into a clean, minimal interface with a clear hierarchy, intuitive flows and consistent visual language. The design focused on reducing friction, ensuring security cues are visible, and making core actions easy to find and complete.

**Business Impact**

Increased User Activation

The simplified onboarding flow led to higher sign-up completion rates and faster time to first transaction.

More Transaction Volume

A cleaner, faster experience encouraged more frequent and higher-value transactions across borders.

Reduced Support Tickets

Clearer guidance and intuitive flows resulted in fewer user errors and less need for customer support.

Stronger Brand Trust

Visible security measures and transparent fees built confidence and long-term loyalty.

**User Experience**

Simple and Intuitive

A clean interface with clear labels and logical flow makes it easy for anyone to send, receive or manage funds.

Faster Access

Key actions are just a tap away, with quick shortcuts for common tasks like deposits, transfers and balance checks.

Greater Control

Real-time balance updates, transaction history and easy wallet management give users full control of their money.

Confident and Secure

Visible security cues, biometric support and trusted payment methods create peace of mind with every transaction.

sections.heading: P2P Trading & Exchange App
sections.body:
I designed a clean interface with clear visual hierarchy, intuitive navigation, and consistent components. The Orders screens make transaction status easy to scan, while currency indicators and structured offer cards help users quickly understand each transaction.

**Key Features**
- P2P NGN ↔ USD exchange flow
- Clear order status: Pending, Completed, Cancelled, and Expired
- Auto-trade transaction indicators
- Structured transaction details and timestamps
- Bottom navigation for quick access to core sections
- Consistent UI components and responsive mobile layouts

**Outcome**

The resulting experience balances clarity, trust, and efficiency, giving users a straightforward way to monitor offers and manage P2P transactions.

The goal was to reduce cognitive load, make verification easy to follow, and build trust while collecting the information required to securely onboard users to Blomgram.

sections.heading: Wallet Flow and Transaction
sections.body:
Designed a scalable fintech wallet and transaction experience, focused on making currency management, trading, and transfers simple and intuitive.

The design prioritizes clear navigation, easy currency selection, transparent transaction details, and reusable components, creating a consistent user experience while providing a flexible foundation for multiple currencies, markets, and future financial services.

Focus: User Experience • Scalability • Trust • Simplicity • Global Expansion

sections.heading: Reflections
sections.body:
**What Worked**

Deploying rapid, atomic component design libraries drastically expedited engineering cycles, ensuring visual alignment from concept straight to finished code in weeks.

**The Challenges**

Integrating our clean interface patterns with legacy financial databases required building advanced middleware strategies to balance low network speeds.

**Lessons Learned**

High-net-worth users prioritize speed and clarity over flashy features. Elegant simplicity will always defeat visual noise when dealing with massive portfolios.

**Areas For Growth**

Future iterations could provide deeper voice-controlled interface states and advanced custom predictive analytics for sophisticated users.

caseStudies.title: Ai-Patient Intake Form
caseStudies.summary:
The AI Patient Intake Form is a web-based healthcare solution designed to make patient onboarding faster, clearer, and less repetitive.

Traditional intake forms often require patients to complete lengthy questionnaires before seeing a healthcare professional. This can lead to incomplete information, repetitive questions, administrative workload, and poor patient experiences.

metadata.platform: UX/UI Design, AI-assisted workflows, Healthcare, Accessibility

cards.title: The Challenge
cards.body:
Patient intake is an important part of the healthcare journey, but conventional forms can create friction for both patients and healthcare providers.

**Patient challenges**
- Long and overwhelming forms
- Repetitive questions
- Unclear medical terminology
- Difficulty knowing which information is relevant
- Poor experience on mobile devices
- Anxiety when providing sensitive information

**Healthcare team challenges**
- Incomplete patient information
- Time spent manually reviewing forms
- Unstructured responses
- Repeated questions during consultations
- Administrative overhead
- Difficulty scaling intake processes across multiple patients

The design opportunity was to create an intake experience that feels simple for patients while producing structured, useful information for healthcare professionals.

cards.title: Product Goal
cards.body:
The goal was to transform patient intake from a static questionnaire into an intelligent, guided experience.

Design objectives

For patients
- Reduce the cognitive load of completing forms
- Make questions easier to understand
- Guide users through the process progressively
- Reduce unnecessary questions
- Clearly communicate progress and next steps

For healthcare teams
- Capture more complete patient information
- Structure responses consistently
- Reduce manual data entry
- Make patient information easier to review
- Support a scalable intake workflow

cards.title: 01 Understand the Intake Journey
cards.body:
I mapped the existing patient journey to identify where users experienced friction.

**The journey was divided into**
**Start → Personal Information → Medical History → Symptoms → Medications → Insurance → Review → Submit.**

Rather than presenting everything on one page, I explored a progressive approach where patients only encounter the information relevant to their current step.

This helped reduce visual and cognitive overload.

cards.title: 02 Design for Progressive Disclosure
cards.body:
One of the core UX decisions was to avoid presenting a long form upfront.

Instead, information is revealed progressively.

**For example**
**What brings you in today?**

After the patient selects a reason for their visit, the system can present relevant follow-up questions.

This creates a more focused experience and prevents patients from answering questions that may not apply to them.

cards.title: 03 Introduce AI Assistance
cards.body:
AI was incorporated as an assistive layer, rather than replacing clinical judgment.

**The AI can help**
- Identify relevant follow-up questions
- Simplify complex terminology
- Detect potentially missing information
- Organize free-text responses
- Summarize information for review
- Adapt the intake flow based on patient responses

cards.title: A guided onboarding experience
cards.body:
The intake flow was designed to feel more like a guided conversation than a traditional administrative form.

**Step 1 — Welcome**

The patient is introduced to the process with a clear explanation of what they will need and approximately how long the intake will take.

Design principle: Reduce uncertainty before asking for information.

cards.title: Step 2 — Personal Information
cards.body:
Essential information such as:
- Full name
- Date of birth
- Contact information
- Address
- Emergency contact

is collected through simple, clearly labelled fields.

cards.title: Step 3 — Reason for Visit
cards.body:
The patient selects or describes why they are seeking care.

The AI uses this information to determine which additional questions may be relevant.

cards.title: Step 4 — Medical History
cards.body:
Instead of presenting a large checklist, information is collected progressively.

**Patients can indicate**
- Existing conditions
- Previous procedures
- Allergies
- Current medications
- Family history

The interface provides contextual explanations where necessary.

cards.title: Step 5 — Symptoms
cards.body:
Patients can describe their symptoms in their own words.

The AI can help structure the response by identifying information such as:
**Symptom → Duration → Severity → Frequency → Related**

**Symptoms**

The patient can then review the captured information before continuing.

cards.title: Step 6 — Review & Confirmation
cards.body:
Before submission, patients receive a summary of their responses.

This gives them an opportunity to:
- Edit incorrect information
- Add missing details
- Confirm important information
- Review what will be shared with the healthcare team

This step builds confidence and reduces avoidable data-entry errors.

caseStudies.title: Sellflo
caseStudies.summary:
E-commerce Management & Creator Collaboration Platform

Sellflo is a digital commerce management platform designed to connect merchants with creators, simplify product promotion, and provide actionable insights into business performance.

The platform enables merchants to manage products, monitor orders, track revenue, and create marketing campaigns, while creators can discover products, participate in affiliate campaigns, monitor clicks and conversions, and track their earnings.
The goal was to design an intuitive, data-driven dashboard that helps both user groups make informed decisions and manage their activities from a centralized workspace.

cards.title: The Challenge
cards.body:
Merchants and creators often need to manage multiple activities across separate tools. Merchants may struggle to monitor sales performance, manage products, and evaluate campaign effectiveness. Creators may find it difficult to identify suitable products, track affiliate links, and understand which promotional activities generate revenue.

**Key Design Challenges**
- Fragmented workflows: Product management, campaign management, and analytics can require switching between different tools.
- Limited visibility: Users need a clear overview of sales, clicks, conversions, and earnings.
- Campaign tracking: Merchants and creators need accessible performance data to evaluate promotional activities.
- Operational complexity: Important actions should be easy to find without overwhelming users with information.
- Different user needs: Merchants and creators require related features but different dashboards and priorities.

cards.title: Product Goal
cards.body:
The goal was to bring commerce management and creator collaboration into a clear, shared workspace with role-specific dashboards.

PROJECT GOALS

The design focused on five primary objectives:
1. Centralize essential commerce and affiliate marketing activities.
2. Make business performance easy to understand at a glance.
3. Simplify product and campaign management.
4. Improve visibility into affiliate clicks, conversions, and earnings.
5. Create a scalable interface that supports both merchants and creators.

sections.heading: Understanding the Users
sections.body: Sellflo serves two primary user groups with different goals and responsibilities.

cards.title: Persona 1: The Merchant
cards.body: Profile: An online business owner or e-commerce operator who wants to increase product visibility and sales through creator partnerships.

cards.title: User Goals
cards.body:
- Add and manage products.
- Create and monitor marketing campaigns.
- Track orders, revenue, and conversions.
- Discover creators to promote products.
- Understand which campaigns generate results.
- Add and manage products.
- Create and monitor marketing campaigns.
- Track orders, revenue, and conversions.
- Discover creators to promote products.
- Understand which campaigns generate results.

cards.title: Pain Points
cards.body:
- Difficulty monitoring multiple business metrics.
- Limited visibility into campaign performance.
- Time-consuming product and order management.
- Difficulty measuring the return on creator partnerships.

Design Opportunity: Provide a unified merchant dashboard with sales analytics, product management, campaign controls, and creator performance insights.

cards.title: Persona 2: The Creator
cards.body: Profile: A content creator or affiliate marketer who promotes products and earns commissions from successful referrals.

cards.title: User Goals
cards.body:
- Discover relevant products to promote.
- Access affiliate links and campaign details.
- Track clicks, conversions, and commissions.
- Monitor payouts and payment status.
- Identify products and campaigns that perform well.

cards.title: Pain Points
cards.body:
- Uncertainty about which promotions convert.
- Difficulty tracking earnings across campaigns.
- Limited transparency into commission and payout status.
- Too many steps between discovering a product and promoting it.

- Design Opportunity: Build a creator-focused workspace that prioritizes product discovery, affiliate link management, performance tracking, and earnings visibility.

cards.title: The Design Strategy
cards.body:
Rather than forcing both audiences into the same experience, Sellflo uses a shared design system with role-specific dashboards.

**Merchant Experience**
- Sales and revenue overview
- Product inventory and management
- Campaign creation and monitoring
- Creator collaboration
- Orders and conversion analytics
- Payout and transaction management

**Creators Experience**
- Recommended products and campaigns
- Affiliate link management
- Clicks and conversion tracking
- Commission and earnings overview
- Payout history
- Campaign performance analytics

sections.body: Clean, utility-focused typographic scales, geometric color spaces, and composable UI blocks.

cards.title: A. Sidebar Navigation
cards.body:
The sidebar groups major features into clearly recognizable sections.

Design rationale: Persistent navigation helps users move between tasks without losing context. Grouping related items also reduces the effort required to locate key features.

**B. Performance Summary Cards**

The dashboard presents high-level metrics such as:
- Total orders
- Total earnings
- Total clicks
- Total conversions

Each card combines a prominent metric, an icon, and a contextual performance indicator.

Design rationale: Users should be able to understand their current performance quickly before exploring detailed analytics.

For merchants, these cards can emphasize orders, sales, and conversions. For creators, the same component can display earnings, clicks, commissions, and conversions.

cards.title: C. Analytics and Visualization
cards.body:
The analytics section uses line and bar charts to communicate changes in performance over time.
- Line charts help users compare clicks, orders, or revenue trends.
- Bar charts help users compare daily earnings, payouts, or campaign activity.
- Tooltips can reveal precise values when users interact with individual data points.

Design rationale: Clear data visualization helps users identify trends and investigate performance changes without navigating through lengthy reports.

**D. Product and Activity Table**

The table displays operational information in a structured format, including product names, locations, dates, quantities, amounts, and statuses.

Design rationale: Tables make detailed records easy to scan, compare, and review. Status indicators help users distinguish completed, pending, and rejected transactions.

For Sellflo, this component can be adapted to show orders for merchants and commission or payout records for creators.

cards.title: E. Quick Actions
cards.body:
The prominent product action in the reference dashboard demonstrates how important tasks can be surfaced directly within the workspace.

Sellflo can extend this approach with actions such as:
- Add Product
- Create Campaign
- Discover Products
- Generate Affiliate Link
- Request Payout

Design rationale: Contextual actions reduce navigation friction and help users complete frequent tasks faster.

sections.body: Show product discovery, affiliate links, conversion analytics, commissions, and payout tracking.

sections.heading: Merchant dashboard
sections.body: Highlight orders, revenue, campaign performance, product management, and merchant-specific quick actions.

caseStudies.title: VPN Medical Appointment Management System
caseStudies.summary: VPN is a medical appointment management application designed to help patients access healthcare appointments while enabling guardians, care teams, agencies, and administrators to coordinate patient care through a centralized digital platform.

metadata.project:
VPN: A multi-role 
healthcare coordination
platform

cards.title: The Challenge
cards.body:
Healthcare appointment coordination can become complicated when patients, guardians, care managers, case managers, agencies, and network administrators rely on different processes to manage the same patient journey.

**Key Design Challenges**

- Potential challenges include:
- Patients struggling to book, confirm, reschedule, or track appointments.
- Guardians needing to coordinate appointments on behalf of dependants.
- Care and case managers requiring visibility into appointments and follow-up actions.
- Agency and network users needing to coordinate services across multiple patients or providers.
- District administrators requiring appropriate oversight without unrestricted access to sensitive patient information.
- Missed appointments, duplicated records, and unclear responsibilities caused by fragmented communication.

The design challenge:

How might we create one connected appointment management experience that gives every user the tools they need without overwhelming them with irrelevant information or exposing data beyond their authorization?

Understanding the users

The platform serves seven distinct user roles. Each role has different responsibilities, permissions, and information needs. A major part of the product design challenge is ensuring that users see the right information and can perform the right actions based on their roles.

cards.title: Research and Discovery
cards.body:
Before designing the interface, I would investigate how appointments are currently requested, approved, scheduled, attended, and followed up.

**Research objectives**
- Understand the existing appointment workflow and its bottlenecks.
- Identify the tasks performed by each of the seven user roles.
- Understand who can book, approve, modify, and cancel appointments.
- Identify information-sharing requirements between patients and authorized representatives.
- Discover how appointment reminders, missed visits, and follow-up actions are handled.
- Map the permissions and reporting requirements at agency, network, and district levels.

cards.title: Key design hypothesis
cards.body:
- The primary problem may not simply be booking an appointment. It may be the lack of a shared, reliable view of what happens before, during, and after that appointment.
- That hypothesis would guide research and be validated before finalizing the solution.

Information architecture

- Dashboard
- Appointments
- Notifications
- Profile and settings

cards.title: Role-specific navigation
cards.body:
- Guardian: Linked patients
- Agency User: Agency appointments and service coordination
- Network User: Network and provider overview
- Care Manager: Assigned patients and follow-ups
- Case Manager: Cases and case-linked appointments
- District Super User: User administration, permissions, configuration, and reports

cards.title: Client (Patient) Dashboard
cards.body:
Dashboard: Upcoming appointments, reminders, and quick actions.

Book Appointment: Select service, provider, date, and time.

My Appointments: View upcoming, completed, cancelled, and missed appointments.

Appointment Details: View location, provider, date, time, and instructions.

Reschedule or Cancel: Modify appointments according to policy.

Notifications: Booking confirmations, reminders, and schedule updates.

Appointment History: Review previous visits and statuses.

Profile and Settings: Manage personal details and communication preferences.

cards.title: Guardian Dashboard
cards.body:
Guardian Dashboard: Overview of linked patients and their upcoming appointments.

Linked Patient Profiles: View and switch between authorized dependants.

Book Appointment: Schedule appointments for a selected patient.

Manage Appointments: View, reschedule, or cancel permitted bookings.

Patient Appointment Details: Access relevant visit information.

Notifications: Receive reminders and updates for linked patients.

Patient History: Review accessible appointment records.

Guardian Profile: Manage personal information and authorization settings.

cards.title: Agency Dashboard
cards.body:
Agency Dashboard: Appointment summaries, pending tasks, and upcoming visits.

Patient Directory: Search and view patients within the agency's scope.

Appointment Management: Create, view, update, or cancel permitted appointments.

Scheduling Calendar: View appointments by date, patient, or provider.

Appointment Status Tracking: Monitor pending, confirmed, completed, and missed visits.

Care Coordination: Manage appointment-related communication and follow-up tasks.

Reports: Review agency appointment activity and operational trends.

Staff and Profile Settings: Manage permitted staff details and agency information.
